data.title: Search the journal on each prompt through a Claude Code hook, not by asking the agent to
data.why: Measured: with search in the instruction files an agent used it 1 time in 10 before the wording said 'before grep' and 0 in 10 after; every run opened with grep over the whole tree. With the hook's output next to the same prompt, 9 in 10 used the journal (6 as the first step), 10 of 10 were right against 9, median context 7.9k tokens against 10.9k, median time 25 s against 44 s (notes on KAD-53). This breaks prime's rule that it is the only thing kadence pushes, on purpose: the pull did not happen. Kept honest by being small - three records, 1 KB at most, silent when the journal has no words for the question, a passage only when its record holds the whole question.
data.rejected: Instruction text alone (a rule line in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and prime): measured, it did not change the first move; A PreToolUse hook that reminds on every grep: fires on legitimate code searches too, and adds a line after the tokens are already spent; Quoting a passage for every hit: a confidently wrong passage makes a model fabricate more than none (DEC-30); titles are pointers, passages only at full coverage
